correctness.rationale: The spectral projectors are exact polynomials in the Laplacian; they yield edge, nonedge and common diagonal entries. Both r and q=(1-r(z))/z are strictly decreasing on positive inputs by explicitly factored rational derivative numerators with positive denominators. All offdiagonal entries are thus strictly positive at all positive times; the common diagonal crosses zero exactly once by monotonicity and endpoint values. A Python stdlib verifier checks 4 polynomial identities, 2945 exact entries, 2670 strict offdiagonals, 275 row sums, and six exact root brackets; the infinite family follows from proof, not finite cases.

value.rationale: A natural complete graph-family criterion gives an exact finite positivity horizon for a commonly used sixth-order diffusion integrator. The universal all-positive off-diagonal law and simultaneous diagonal failure are structurally stronger than a numerical threshold table. Unlike the fourth-order method, sixth-order has finite positivity horizon even for C4, making the nonmonotone order-versus-positivity tradeoff explicit and useful for safe timesteps.
